ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the lower left of the circuit diagram there is an NMOS current mirror driven by a 1 mA reference current, with the reference transistor labeled W/L=2 and mirrored to the tail current transistor labeled W/L=3. In the middle is an NMOS differential pair, and both input transistors are labeled W/L=5, with the left input as V1 and the right input as V2. Above is a PMOS active load/mirror structure; the right-side control PMOS is labeled W/L=10, and its gate is connected to the gate of the far-right output PMOS; the far-right output PMOS is labeled W/L=40, and the output current Iout is downward. Reasoning: The reference branch current is 1 mA. Since the size ratio of the output transistor to the reference transistor in the tail current mirror is (W/L)_out/(W/L)_ref = 3/2, when channel-length modulation and body effect are ignored, the tail current is 1 mA × 3/2 = 1.5 mA. Given V1=0 and V2=Vdd, all the differential-pair current is directed to the right input branch, the left branch current is 0, and the right branch current is 1.5 mA. Therefore the right-side W/L=10 PMOS control branch carries 1.5 mA. The far-right output PMOS has the same gate-source bias as this PMOS, and the current is mirrored in proportion to W/L, so Iout = 1.5 mA × (40/10) = 6.0 mA. Expressed to 1 decimal place, it is 6.0 mA.

Image description: The circuit diagram shows a 1 mA reference branch from Vdd feeding a diode-connected NMOS labeled W/L=2, with its gate connected to another NMOS labeled W/L=3 that acts as the tail current device. Above it is a differential NMOS pair, each input transistor labeled W/L=5, with gates marked V1 on the left and V2 on the right. The drains of these input NMOS devices connect to PMOS loads tied to Vdd, each labeled W/L=10. On the right, the W/L=10 PMOS gate connection is also tied to a separate PMOS output device labeled W/L=40, whose drain current is marked Iout downward.

Reasoning: The 1 mA through the diode-connected W/L=2 NMOS establishes a reference VGS. The W/L=3 NMOS has the same VGS, so ignoring channel length modulation and body effect, the mirrored tail current scales by W/L ratio: Itail = 1 mA × (3/2) = 1.5 mA. Given V1 = 0, the left NMOS input transistor is cut off. Given V2 = Vdd, the right NMOS input transistor conducts, so the full 1.5 mA tail current flows through the right branch. Therefore the right W/L=10 PMOS load carries 1.5 mA. The output PMOS has the same VSG as this right W/L=10 PMOS but has W/L=40, so its current is scaled by 40/10 = 4. Hence Iout = 4 × 1.5 mA = 6.0 mA.
